title: Thankful or Grumbling?
retry: Listen once more and choose a pile.

items.text: You say thank you when someone pours your water.
items.note: Your words notice the person who helped you.

items.text: You say this cup is stupid because it is not blue.
items.note: You can ask for blue without insulting the cup you received.

items.text: You thank God for dinner before you eat.
items.note: We can thank God for the food in front of us.

items.text: You shove your gift away and call it junk.
items.note: You can treat a gift gently even when it is not your favourite.

items.text: You thank your teacher for reading your book.
items.note: Your teacher gave time to read with you.

items.text: You complain that your friend got a bigger sticker.
items.note: You can enjoy your sticker without measuring your friend’s.

items.text: You tell Grandma you enjoyed the time together.
items.note: Thankfulness can name time together as a gift.

items.text: You throw your crayons because the box is small.
items.note: A small box still gives you colours to draw with.

items.text: You say thank you for a warm coat.
items.note: Your coat helps keep you warm.

items.text: You call dinner yucky before you sit down.
items.note: You can speak kindly about the food someone prepared.

items.text: You thank God for the trees on your walk.
items.note: We can notice what God made and thank Him.

items.text: You groan at every toy because you want a new one.
items.note: You can look for something to enjoy among the toys you have.

items.text: You thank a friend for sharing a ball.
items.note: Your friend made room for you to play.

items.text: You say thank you for dinner and ask for water because your mouth feels hot.
items.note: You can be thankful and still ask for what your body needs.

items.text: You say thanks for the gift and then call it the worst gift ever.
items.note: The insult takes away the kindness of your thank you.

items.text: You tell God you feel sad and thank Him for listening.
items.note: You can tell God the truth about your feelings.

items.text: You thank your grown-up for your shoes and say they hurt your toes.
items.note: You can thank someone and still tell them that something hurts.

items.text: You thank your friend for inviting you even though the game is over.
items.note: You can be disappointed and still notice your friend’s kindness.
